KEY MESSAGE 1...A Noreaster will continue to impact the region 
with much of our area impacts in Downeast Maine through Tuesday 
AM; bringing breezy NE winds, and periods of rain.

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...
The center of low pressure (at 1004mb) associated with this 
Noreaster is beginning to drift NE this morning. As of 1AM EDT
the center was approx 50mi east of Ocean City, NJ and drifting
NE as it begins to get picked up by the westerlies. A large 
occlusion is wrapped up to near Cape Cod with a triple point 
near Georges Bank. Satellite imagery is showing moisture 
advecting north in Maine from the the Atlantic which extends 
back to the Bahamas. This has increased PWATs over Downeast 
Maine into the 175-200 percent of normal range for late 
September. This system is nearly vertically stacked with the
500mb low aloft and a significant amount of dry air has worked
into the Gulf of Maine noted by GOES-East 7.34um water vapor
imagery. A large blossom of precipitation north of the triple
point over the Gulf of Maine is pushing into the Downeast at
this update. This is associated with an area of upper level
divergence increasing surface convergence which has resulted in
an area of positive 1000-925mb frontogenesis. This has resulted
in moderate to brief heavy bursts of rain in Downeast Maine.
Latest RAP Mesoscale Analysis data suggests 250-400j/kg of
MUCAPE over the Gulf of Maine waters may advect into the area.
Have opted to add isolated thunder to the forecast for the next
few hours with this blossom of precip over the waters and
Downeast coast to near Bangor region. 

At the same time a strong 1028mb high pressure system
sits over Eastern Quebec near Labrador with a 583dam 500mb 
ridge. The placement of the ridge and North Atlantic low 
pressure near Greenland is preventing this Noreaster from moving
too fast at this point but the ridge is collapsing which is
allowing this cutoff Noreaster begin to return into the
westerlies and getting pulled north thanks to an approach trof
in Ontario. The global models and hi-res guidance is in fairly 
good agreement for today. The approaching trof in Central 
Ontario will begin to pull the Noreaster in a NE direction over 
Southern New England this afternoon and cross the Gulf of Maine 
waters tomorrow and exit east of Nova Scotia on Wednesday AM. 
The surface low today will continue to slowly weaken and then 
weaken to a 1011mb low over the Gulf of Maine tomorrow and 
1015mb by Wednesday AM. Here is what to expect for the various 
components of the storm:

Periods of Rain...The forecasting challenge today is noted via
the hi-res CAMs and globals on how to handle all this dry air
wrapping into the system. Current thinking is the placement of
upper level divergence keeps the CWA in a favorable area for
surface lift and therefore periods of light to moderate rain
today favoring the southern 1/2 of the CWA. However, by late in
the day light rain likely to reach portions of Northern Maine
but significant uncertainty with how much stays together running
into the surface high dry dome to our north. Confidence is high
enough to keep chance to likely POPs across the area today with
highest POPs from the Central Highlands southward to Downeast
coast. But do not be surprised if there is a period of dry
conditions with just low clouds until another area of rain
rotates over any particular location. Unfortunately event total
precipitation has trended down once again with this forecast 
update. Looking at event totals (through Tue AM) of 0.6-0.8 inch
for areas from Dover-Foxcroft to Danforth and points southward.
An area of 1-1.5 inch possible from Bangor to Bar Harbor thanks
to this mornings heavier precip. Moosehead Region to Baxter to 
Houlton only looking at 0.3-0.5 inch totals and north of there 
to the St. John Valley just a Trace to 0.25 inch possible. Tons 
of uncertainty with Northern Maine thanks to the dry air this 
system has to continue to fight through. We do not expect any 
flooding concerns anywhere given the D1-D3 drought conditions. 
In fact nearly all of the rainfall will likely be absorbed into 
the near surface ground and very unlikely any water gets into 
the rivers and streams. Rivers and streams are currently in the 
1-15th percentile range with many approaching top 5 lowest flows
on record. 

Breezy Winds...As the low pressure weakens today into Tuesday
the pressure gradient between the Maritimes high and this
Noreaster continues to weaken. NE winds today mainly for the
Bangor Region to Downeast coast may gust 20-25mph especially
this morning with some gusts to 30mph on the islands and Downeast
coastline exposed to the NE winds across the open waters. We 
don't anticipate impacts from the wind other than maybe a very 
few isolated power outages Downeast.
